delivery-dependencies.text: The roadmap diagram shows three contract workstreams: roots and proofs, sessions and history, and availability and switching. Commitment and session contracts inform CSMT-UTXO measurements. These measured capabilities and service contracts feed the complete journey before component delivery is assigned. The table gives each workstream a concrete deliverable and an exit criterion.

settle-the-chainpoint-contract.text: Specify acquisition, leases, rollback, eviction and history coverage with a reviewed executable model and simulation. The exit evidence includes explicit refusals and no silent chainpoint substitution. Cryptographic assumptions remain separate.

specify-the-trust-and-availability-offer.text: Define both own-anchor and institutional-publication choices, with root acceptance separate from data delivery. The exit contract specifies the verification boundary for both untrusted services and observable availability promises.

measure-the-ledger-engine.text: Start with the linked CSMT-UTXO engine, benchmark paths and metrics. Measure anchor validation and current commitment costs separately from archive storage, retained views and query or proof serving. Bind results to the actual workload and configuration.

demonstrate-one-complete-journey.text: The second diagram keeps one accepted root and chainpoint while the terminal checks equivalent ledger claims from two providers and proofs from an untrusted application builder. Valid links yield an application claim; failed evidence is rejected before action. Demonstrate provider switching, nested roots, wrong roots, missing history and expired sessions, with test publishers explicitly labelled.

assign-implementation-work.text: Map the agreed contracts and demonstration evidence to anchor, ledger, application and terminal owners. Each role has a separate acceptance boundary. Reconcile existing CSMT issues explicitly; this plan neither moves those issues nor releases paused work.

delivery-status.text: This bootstrap creates a design record and documentation checks only. Existing paused implementation work remains paused; no production service or product release is launched.
